title: Accessibility: any library image put in a vignette field renders with alt="" and loses its caption/crop; the library's required alt never reaches the page
claim: noteFor is keyed by committed manifest ids only. Vignette fields (started/built movements, built intro) store a bare id and StoryFigure takes alt, caption, ratio and focus from noteFor. Once Anas replaces a vignette with a library image, the loader hands over a `media|...` reference (or a bare uuid), which is not in MEDIA_NOTES, so alt is '' and the photo is treated as decorative. The media table has `alt_ar text not null` (uploads require alt), but mediaById selects only `id,derivatives` and anon has only `grant select (id, derivatives)`, so the alt cannot be used. PostView also hardcodes alt="" for post covers (src/components/public/journal/PostView.tsx:51).
failure_scenario: The owner swaps the 'raha-poster-orange' vignette in the built room for a newly uploaded photo of a branch. It publishes with no description: screen-reader users get an unlabeled image (WCAG 1.1.1) although a Arabic alt was entered at upload, and the 4:5 crop and caption of the old image are gone.
suggested_fix: grant select (alt_ar) on public.media to anon, select `id,derivatives,alt_ar` in mediaById, carry alt with the resolved reference (or add an `alt` field next to each vignette in the room schemas) and make noteFor/StoryFigure and PostView use it when the id has no MEDIA_NOTES entry.

title: Clip-path wipe keyframes have no `to` state, so every CSS entrance wipe is a 50% snap, not a wipe
claim: motion-band, motion-media and motion-sign declare only a `from` clip-path and rely on the element's own style as the end state. The element's own clip-path is `none`, and `none` cannot be interpolated with `inset()`, so Chromium animates it discretely: fully clipped until the eased progress reaches 50%, then everything appears at once. Verified in Chromium 153 with the same keyframes: from-only at 25% gives `inset(0px 0px 0px 100%)` and at 75% gives `none`; the same animation with an explicit `to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0) }` gives `inset(0px 0px 0px 75%)` and `inset(0px 0px 0px 25%)`. The opacity/transform keyframes (`motion-rise`, `motion-fade`) interpolate fine. DESIGN.md:139 documents `band` as a wipe in the reading direction, `media` as a wipe upward, `sign` as the signature written left to right, and DESIGN.md:142 says the home portrait has a 500ms wipe. motion.ts is correct because its TO table has explicit end states, so only the CSS `data-enter` entrances are broken. No test checks clip-path.
failure_scenario: Open `/` at 1440. The three h1 name bands use `enter(60 + i*140, 'band')` (900ms, ease-weave) and stay fully clipped until about 450ms after their delay, then pop in whole. The portrait (`enter(0,'media')`, `--enter-dur: 500ms`, the largest first-screen picture, fetchPriority high) is invisible for about 250ms then pops. On /book the cover (`enter(240,'media')`, 1100ms) is invisible for about 790ms; the signature (`sign`, 1800ms) appears at about 900ms. No wipe is ever seen, and first-screen content shows later than designed.
suggested_fix: Give each keyframe an explicit end: `@keyframes motion-band { from { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 100%) } to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0) } }`, likewise motion-media (`inset(100% 0 0 0)` to `inset(0 0 0 0)`) and motion-sign (`inset(0 100% 0 0)` to `inset(0 0 0 0)`). Keep fill-mode `backwards` so no clip lingers after the end. Apply the same fix to the other from-only clip-path keyframes (site.module.css menu-weave, scenes.module.css tile-in, viewer-in, photo-next, photo-prev).

title: Alt text edited in the admin is ignored for the moonlight cup photos, and library images publish with empty alt
claim: `moon.images` is a list of `{ id, alt }` (galleryPhotoFields, src/admin/collections/rooms.ts:38-41, alt required). The renderer uses `moon.images[0]` and `[1]` with their `.alt`, but passes the third and fourth to StoryFigure by id only. StoryFigure takes its alt from the hard-coded media-notes table (`noteFor(id)`, Story.tsx:77), which returns `{ alt: '' }` for any id it does not list. Separately, a media-library image resolves to a `media|…` reference string and its required `alt_ar` is never fetched: `mediaById` selects only `id,derivatives` (src/lib/content.ts:72). So any library image put in a room's `vignette` field, or in place of those two photos, is published as `alt=""` (decorative) although the library made Anas write a description.
failure_scenario: Anas opens «على الرف», rewrites the alt of the factory-mug photo (or swaps in a library image whose alt he typed) and publishes. The public page still says «كوب ضوء القمر الأصفر بزهوره المرسومة في المصنع» for the old photo, or renders the new one with alt="", so screen-reader users get no description. His edit has no effect and nothing tells him.
suggested_fix: Pass `alt={moonFactory.alt}` (and the `{moonInside}` equivalent) through StoryFigure, falling back to noteFor(id) only for caption/link. For bare `vignette` ids, add `alt_ar` to the `mediaById` select and carry it in the resolved reference, or add an alt field beside each vignette.

title: A blank journal menu label blanks the journal's name everywhere (?? does not catch '')
claim: getJournalName falls back to «المجلس» only when the nav item is missing. The nav `label` field is a plain text field with no nonBlank rule, so the publish gate accepts an empty label, and `'' ?? 'المجلس'` stays ''. tests/unit/content-loaders.test.ts covers the rename and the missing item but not a blank label.
failure_scenario: Anas clears the label of the /journal menu item (or saves it as spaces) and publishes. The header link, the journal page h1 and <title>, the home door, the 404 list and the post breadcrumb all render with no text: empty link names for screen readers and an empty heading.
suggested_fix: Use `const label = ...?.label.trim(); return label || 'المجلس'`, and add nonBlank: true to navItemFields.label so the gate refuses it too.

title: Committed totalBytes no longer matches the listed films after the five child films were removed
claim: AUDIT-1 G4.2 removed the five child films from this manifest by hand. `videos` now lists 13 films whose bytes sum to 41,697,224 (each entry matches its file on disk), but totalBytes still says 58588162, a difference of 16,890,938. scripts/prepare-media.mjs computes totalBytes from the same list, so the committed file is not what the script would write. Nothing reads totalBytes today, but ISSUES P11 asks the owner to decide about committing or uploading these films and this is the number a reader will use.
failure_scenario: The P11 decision on whether the 13 films fit the hosting budget uses 58.6 MB instead of 41.7 MB; a rerun of prepare-media.mjs also produces a diff in a file that looked final.
suggested_fix: Rerun scripts/prepare-media.mjs, or set totalBytes to 41697224.

title: Misspelled Arabic in the public consulting copy
claim: The consulting intro and one service text carry orthography errors on a public business page: «الإستشارة» (should be «الاستشارة»), «الاتقان» («الإتقان») and «المتابعه» («المتابعة»). The same class appears in content/initial-content.json (for example «تفصيله صغيره» line 115, «والإحتفاظ» line 116, «انشاء» line 52, «صدفه» line 177), where D39 treats the words as Anas's own; check:copy checks only digits and placeholders.
quote: نقدم الإستشارة العملية لوضع أساس لمشروعك
failure_scenario: A prospective client reads the services section of /contact and sees a misspelled word in the first sentence describing a paid consulting offer.
suggested_fix: Correct the three spellings in contact.ts after Anas approves (the file says its scope is his to confirm); raise the initial-content.json ones with him, since the seed publishes them.

title: Passed room drops a story picture entirely when the text has fewer blocks than pictures
claim: Every id in STORY_PICTURES that exists in the gallery is removed from the products mosaic (`shownProducts`). A picture is only drawn beside text while `pictures[text++]` has a text block to sit beside (line 62). The number of text blocks is one more than the number of matched band lines. If fewer than two text blocks exist, the unused picture is in neither place. BuiltRoomView explicitly solved this class of problem (S13.2: 'drawn exactly once, whatever band lines the owner sets'); Passed did not get the same treatment.
failure_scenario: The owner corrects one character in the band paragraph «مررتُ بها… ومرّت بي» but leaves the `bandLines` entry as it was. The band no longer matches, `toBlocks` yields a single text block, and `pictures[0]` (31-murady-french-toast-banana) is used. `28-gold-tarts` is filtered out of `shownProducts` and never rendered, so a published product photo silently disappears. Nothing in the admin or the publish gate reports it.
suggested_fix: Exclude from `shownProducts` only the pictures actually drawn: compute the text-block count from `blocks` first and use `pictures.slice(0, textBlockCount)` in the filter.

title: Built room poster is still dropped when the first band has no text after it
claim: S13.2 was fixed so that the poster (`room.intro.vignette`) is 'drawn exactly once, whatever band lines the owner sets'. The fix covers 0 band lines and 2 band lines. It misses a band line that is the last block of the intro. In that case `texts.find((i) => i > firstBand)` is undefined, `posterAt` is undefined, and no TextRun receives the figure.
quote: const posterAt = firstBand === -1 ? texts[texts.length - 1] : texts.find((i) => i > firstBand)
failure_scenario: The owner moves the band line to the final paragraph of the intro, a natural place for a dramatic line. `intro` becomes [text, band]; `firstBand` is 1 and there is no text index greater than 1. `posterAt` is undefined, so the «دعوة من رحى المكان» poster is never rendered on /built, contradicting the comment above it.
suggested_fix: Fall back to the last text before the band: `texts.find((i) => i > firstBand) ?? texts[texts.length - 1]`.

title: «اطلب جلسة» swaps the message but keeps the submission key, so a lost-response retry reports a message as sent that was never stored
claim: `update()` sets `submissionKey.current = null` on every edit, so a changed message always gets a new key. The service-event handler replaces the message without doing that. `contact_submit` looks the key up first and returns `duplicate: true` when it exists, without comparing the message. The edge function turns that into `received()` (201). So a different message under an old key is acknowledged and dropped. The S16.5 fix (replace an untouched prefill) is what created this path: before it, a non-empty message was never replaced by the event.
quote: setValues((v) => ({ ...v, message: v.message.trim() && v.message !== previous ? v.message : text }))
failure_scenario: The visitor clicks «اطلب جلسة» on «بناء القائمة» and sends the untouched prefill. The server stores it under key K, but the response is lost (network drop), so the form shows 'تعذّر الاتصال' and keeps K for the retry. The visitor then clicks «اطلب جلسة» on «حساب التكلفة»; the message equals the previous prefill, so it is replaced. Pressing أرسل sends the new text with K; the server sees K, returns 201, and the form says «وصلت رسالتك. شكراً لك.» The «حساب التكلفة» request was never stored and Anas never sees it. Needs a lost response first, so it is rare.
suggested_fix: When the handler actually replaces the message, also set `submissionKey.current = null`.

title: The admin's alt text for the moonlight-cup factory and inside photos is accepted and ignored
claim: `moon.images` entries have an editable `alt` (galleryPhotoFields). The render and second render use it (`alt={moonRender.alt}`, `alt={moonRender2.alt}`). The factory and inside photos go through `StoryFigure`, which takes alt only from the hard-coded MEDIA_NOTES table keyed by the seed image id. Story.tsx documents this for fields that have no alt of their own, but these two fields do have one.
failure_scenario: The owner replaces the factory-mug photo with a new library image and writes its description in the admin's «الوصف البديل» box. `noteFor(id)` finds no note for the new id and returns `{ alt: '' }`. The photo is published with alt="" (decorative) and no caption, and the alt the owner typed is never used. Screen-reader users get no description of a content photo, and the admin shows a field that does nothing. The same applies to `moonInside` at line 248.
suggested_fix: Add an optional `alt` prop to StoryFigure that wins over `note.alt`, and pass `alt={moonFactory.alt}` and `alt={moonInside.alt}`.

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: Built movements have an image and a «صورة عريضة» switch in the admin that the page never reads
claim: builtMovementFields (src/admin/collections/rooms.ts:75-77) offers `vignette` and `vignetteWide` on every movement. Nothing in src reads `movement.vignette` for a built room (a grep for `.vignette` finds only `room.intro.vignette` here and the started room's movement). The seed even sets `vignetteWide: true` on the branches movement. The text of both movements is drawn without any picture.
failure_scenario: The owner picks a photo for the branches movement and ticks «صورة عريضة». The draft preview and the published /built page show no photo and no change. The owner cannot tell whether the save failed or the field is dead.
suggested_fix: Either render `branches.vignette` and `team.vignette` beside the movement text (using vignetteWide for the layout), or remove the two fields from builtMovementFields so the admin does not offer them.

title: Band and pull lines are matched by exact text and nothing checks they still match a paragraph
claim: `classify` keeps `pullLines` and `bandLines` as separate copies of paragraph text and matches them with `Set.has`. rooms.ts:14-16 says each 'must repeat a paragraph exactly', but no room schema has a superRefine, and no SQL touches bandLines or pullLines (both checked by grep). Editing a paragraph without editing its copy silently turns a band or large line into a plain paragraph. That changes how many text blocks exist, and the views assume that count: PassedRoomView loses a picture (see the PassedRoomView finding), and ShelfRoomView draws `moonRender2` and `moonInside` only when `splitClosing` finds a display line at index 2 or later.
failure_scenario: The owner fixes a typo in the moonlight cup's two large lines ('ومن ذلك الحلم ولدت هذه المجموعة' and 'لأن بعض الأحلام الصغيرة…') but not in pullLines. `splitClosing` gets no display line after index 0, returns `[paras, []]`, `moonLast` is empty, and the second render and the inside-of-the-cup photo vanish from /shelf. Publish succeeds with no warning.
suggested_fix: Add a superRefine to the four room schemas: every `pullLines` and `bandLines` entry must equal one of that room's paragraphs (started: any movement's paragraphs). Refuse publish with a message naming the stray line.

title: html scroll-behavior:smooth without data-scroll-behavior makes every route change scroll-animate from the old offset
claim: Next 16.3.5 only forces `scroll-behavior:auto` during a route transition when `<html>` has `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` (node_modules/next/dist/shared/lib/router/utils/disable-smooth-scroll.js). Without the attribute it runs `fn()` untouched, and layout-router.js then does `htmlElement.scrollTop = 0`, which this CSS turns into a smooth scroll. src/app/(public)/layout.tsx:31 renders `<html lang="ar" dir="rtl">` with no such attribute (grep finds none in src), so the dev server also warns on every navigation.
failure_scenario: On any room page the visitor scrolls to the bottom and clicks the RoomNav «الغرفة التالية» door or a footer link. The new page is committed at the old scroll offset (clamped), then the browser glides up to the top over roughly a second while the new page's entrances play. MotionLayer's scan runs at the old offset, so the first-screen reveals are skipped as 'above the fold'. It affects the main way of moving between rooms.
suggested_fix: Add `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` to the `<html>` element in src/app/(public)/layout.tsx (and the admin layout if it loads globals.css). In-page anchors and SectionNav links keep their smooth scroll.

title: menu-weave has no `to` clip-path, so the menu opens empty and its bands pop in instead of wiping
claim: Same root cause as the motion.css keyframes. `.menu[open] .menuLink` runs `menu-weave` with `backwards` fill and `calc(var(--i) * 45ms)` delay. The keyframe has only `from { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 100%) }` and the end state is `none`, so Chromium treats it as discrete (verified: stays fully clipped until 50% of the eased time, then `none`).
failure_scenario: On a phone the visitor taps «القائمة». The dialog opens showing only the top bar on the aubergine backdrop. Each of the 60px+ bands stays invisible for roughly 280ms (`--dur-base` 560ms halved) plus `i * 45ms`, then appears at once, so the last band (i up to 6-7) shows at about 600ms. It reads as lag, not as the woven wipe DESIGN.md describes.
suggested_fix: Add `to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0) }` to menu-weave.

title: tile-in, viewer-in, photo-next and photo-prev are from-only clip-path animations (discrete flip at 50%)
claim: tile-in (line 61), viewer-in (150), photo-next (200) and photo-prev (205) each declare only `from { clip-path: ... }`. The end state is `clip-path: none`, which does not interpolate with `inset()`, so each snaps at 50% of its eased duration (verified in Chromium 153). The lightbox 'opens with a wipe' and a photo 'step' from DESIGN.md:142 are therefore a delayed appearance.
failure_scenario: Open /scenes: each tile is clipped away for about 350ms plus `min(i,10) * 45ms` and then pops in. Open a photo: the dialog shows only the aub-900 backdrop for about 140ms, then the whole viewer appears. Press the next arrow: the new photo is invisible for about 140ms, then appears, so each step blinks instead of wiping.
suggested_fix: Add an explicit `to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0) }` to all four keyframes (same fix as motion.css).

title: ::selection colours equal the aubergine band colours, so selected text is invisible on aub bands
claim: `::selection` paints `--aub` background with `--sand-50` text globally. On `data-tone="aub"` the band is `--bg: var(--aub)` with `--fg: var(--sand-50)`, i.e. exactly the same pair, so selection changes nothing. There are 25 `tone="aub"` bands, and the footer (`<footer data-tone="aub">`) is on every public page. On night and deep bands the difference is about 1.2:1. No other `::selection` rule exists for the site (the only one is in the book reader).
failure_scenario: A visitor selects the footer poem or the home statement band to copy or read it aloud. Nothing is highlighted, so they cannot tell what was selected or whether the drag worked.
suggested_fix: Make the selection tone-aware, e.g. `::selection { background: var(--fg); color: var(--bg); }`, which inverts on every band, or give dark tones an explicit saffron selection.

title: .motion-scrub > * also animates Figure's corner caption
claim: Figure.tsx:38 puts the `motion-scrub` class on the frame, and the frame contains both the `<picture>` and the absolutely placed `<figcaption class=corner>`. `.motion-scrub > *` therefore applies the scroll-linked `scale(1.16) -> scale(1.06)` and `translateY` to the caption as well as the image. The doc comment describes the class as 'an image frame that zooms out slowly'. The combination is real: PassedRoomView.tsx:112 (product brand captions «ارم», «مرادي») and BookView.tsx:153 (photo captions) both use `scrub` with `captionPlacement="corner"`.
failure_scenario: On /passed in a browser with scroll timelines, the brand label on each product tile grows to 1.16x (15px text becomes about 17px) when the tile enters and shrinks to 1.06x as it scrolls, while its bottom and inline-start edges are pushed against the frame's overflow:hidden. The label looks like it breathes as the page scrolls.
suggested_fix: Scope the rule to the image: `.motion-scrub > picture { ... }` (Figure and the journal/home figures all wrap the image in `<picture>`), or render the corner caption outside the scrubbed frame.

title: Section links' focus ring is clipped top and bottom by the scroller
claim: `.scroller` sets `overflow-x:auto`, which computes `overflow-y` to `auto` (checked in Chromium). `.list` has `padding-block:0` and `.link` is exactly 54px tall, so the scroller is 54px high. `.link` has no data-tone and no focus rule, so it gets the global `:focus-visible` ring (3px outline, 3px offset), which lies 3px to 6px outside the link box and is clipped by the scroller at the top and bottom. Only the two side bars remain. Elsewhere the code moves rings inside for exactly this reason (`[data-tone]:is(a,button)`, `.play`, `.captionLink a`).
failure_scenario: A keyboard user tabs through «أقسام الكتاب» on /book. Each link shows only two vertical saffron bars, no top or bottom edge, on a 54px strip, which is a weak indicator against the aubergine bar.
suggested_fix: Draw the ring inside: `.link:focus-visible { outline-offset: -6px }`, or give `.list` block padding of at least 6px.

title: The film's own focus ring is fully clipped, so the focus VideoTile moves to it has no visible indicator
claim: VideoTile.tsx:70 moves focus to the `<video>` when playback starts. `.video` fills `.tile`, which has `overflow:hidden`, and gets the global `:focus-visible` ring drawn 3px outside its box (there is no `.video:focus-visible` rule and no data-tone), so the whole ring is clipped. `.play` was given an inside ring for the same reason, but the video was not.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user presses Enter on «تشغيل». The button unmounts and focus lands on the `<video>`, but nothing shows where focus is until the next Tab reaches a native control. Space or K works on an element the user cannot see is focused.
suggested_fix: Add `.video:focus-visible { outline-offset: -6px; }` (tone colour comes from the band; `--focus` is inherited).

title: An AbortError from the visitor's own pause is reported as a playback failure
claim: `start()` sets state 'playing' (native controls appear) and then calls `play()`. With `preload="none"` the promise stays pending until data arrives. If the visitor presses pause in that window, the browser rejects the promise with AbortError ('interrupted by a call to pause()'). The catch handler sets 'failed' regardless of the reason. The film itself is fine. This is separate from AUDIT-1 S13.5, whose fix (always-mounted status region) holds.
failure_scenario: On a slow mobile connection the visitor taps «تشغيل» on the 5.8 MB raha-reel film, sees the controls, and taps pause before the first bytes arrive. `state` becomes 'failed': the controls are removed, the play button returns and «تعذّر تشغيل المقطع. حاول مرة أخرى.» is announced, though nothing failed.
suggested_fix: Ignore the abort: `.catch((error) => { if (error?.name !== 'AbortError') setState('failed') })`.

title: .lattice paints its solid --line colour into unfilled cells; two 3-item lattices leave an aubergine hole at tablet widths
claim: `.lattice` uses `background: var(--line)` for its 1px seams, and that background also fills any empty grid cell. Other lattices append a weave filler (JournalList.tsx:82, ShelfRoomView.tsx:189, PassedRoomView.tsx:54; scenes.module.css:44 says 'A row that does not fill shows the weave, as B's lattices end'). BookView.tsx:182 (`.objects`, 3 items, `--tile:240px`) and ShelfRoomView.tsx:74 (`.doors`, 3 items, `--tile:280px`) have no filler. At a 768px viewport the content width is about 689px, so auto-fit gives 2 columns for both and the third item sits alone in row 2.
failure_scenario: On an iPad-portrait viewport (768 to about 805px on /book, 625 to about 935px on /shelf) the last row is one card plus a solid aubergine rectangle the size of a card, instead of the woven cell used everywhere else.
suggested_fix: Add a `weave` filler cell (aria-hidden li with the existing weaveCell style) to those two lists, or make `.lattice > :last-child:nth-child(...)` fillers a shared class in layout.module.css that paints weave.svg instead of solid ink.

title: The current-room and current-section triangles vanish in forced-colors mode
claim: The only visual cue for `aria-current` is a triangle drawn with `background: currentColor` (site.module.css `.here` line 68, `.menuHere` line 172) or `background: var(--coral)` (section-nav.module.css:67). In forced-colors mode Chromium replaces `background-color` with the system Canvas colour. Checked with forcedColors emulation: a `background:currentColor` triangle on a sand page computes to rgb(255,255,255), the same as the page, so it is invisible. action.module.css and signature.module.css already have forced-colors handling for their decorative shapes, but these state cues do not.
failure_scenario: A sighted Windows High Contrast user opens the header on /book. No link shows which room they are in, and SectionNav shows no current section, because the triangle has become Canvas on Canvas.
suggested_fix: Add `@media (forced-colors: active) { .here, .menuHere { forced-color-adjust: none; background: CanvasText; } }` in site.module.css and the same for `.here` in section-nav.module.css.

title: The pressed filter is shown only by a background swap, which forced-colors mode erases
claim: `.filter[aria-pressed='true']` differs from the unpressed state only by `background` and `color`. Checked with forcedColors emulation in Chromium: a pressed button computes to background rgb(255,255,255) and an unpressed one to transparent white on a white page, both with black text, so they look the same. scenes.module.css:20 has the identical rule. Both filters are visible only when scripting is enabled.
failure_scenario: A Windows High Contrast user on /journal or /scenes clicks a category. The list changes, but no filter button shows which one is active, so they cannot tell the current filter or how to get back to «الكل».
suggested_fix: Add to both files: `@media (forced-colors: active) { .filter[aria-pressed='true'] { background: Highlight; color: HighlightText; forced-color-adjust: none; } }`, or add a border or underline on the pressed state.

title: The intro picture is dropped when the first band line is the last block of the intro
claim: The S13.2 fix claims (lines 85-87) that the film and the poster are each "drawn exactly once, whatever band lines the owner sets". posterAt is texts.find((i) => i > firstBand), which is undefined when no text block follows the first band. This happens when the owner marks the intro's last paragraph as a band line, which the admin allows. Then no TextRun gets figure={room.intro.vignette}, and the poster is never rendered at all. The other two cases, no band and a mid-intro band, work.
quote: const posterAt = firstBand === -1 ? texts[texts.length - 1] : texts.find((i) => i > firstBand)
failure_scenario: In the admin, Anas adds the final intro paragraph to bandLines. intro becomes [text, band]. firstBand is 1, texts is [0], and posterAt is undefined. The page shows the film under the band but the vignette picture has disappeared from /built.
suggested_fix: Fall back to the last text when none follows the band: `texts.find((i) => i > firstBand) ?? texts[texts.length - 1]`.

title: Admin draft preview of a post still shows the stock «المجلس» crumb after the journal is renamed
claim: The G3.1 fix makes the journal name editable (D11) through getJournalName(). PostView defaults journalName to 'المجلس', and the only caller that omits it is the admin's draft preview (RoomPreview.tsx:69). The published page and the preview then disagree, although shapePost was introduced so they cannot differ.
quote: export function PostView({ post, journalName = 'المجلس' }: { post: JournalPost; journalName?: string }) {
failure_scenario: Anas renames the menu item to «المدونة». The live post page shows «→ المدونة» in the crumbs. His draft preview of the next post still shows «→ المجلس», so he cannot check the real header.
suggested_fix: Have the admin preview read the /journal nav label from the site settings it already loads and pass it as journalName, or at least pass the same value BookView's preview gets.

title: A blank menu label passes publish and blanks the journal's name on every page
claim: navItemFields declares label and href as plain `text`, so publish accepts an empty string (`nonBlank` exists since S11.3 but is applied only in the catalog tables). getJournalName falls back with `??`, which does not catch ''. The empty name feeds the journal page's h1 and title, the post pages' back link and the book page's link. The menu itself shows a link with no name. The same holds for home.name, room titles and taglines.
failure_scenario: Anas clears the «المجلس» label in the settings menu list, meaning to retype it, and publishes. The schema passes. After the rebuild /journal has an empty h1 and an empty <title>, and the menu shows a nameless link.
suggested_fix: Set `nonBlank: true` on the nav item label and href, home.name and the room title fields. Use `||` in getJournalName so an empty label falls back to «المجلس».

title: Journal category filter changes the list without any announcement
claim: The scenes gallery announces how many photos a filter left through an always-mounted role=status element (AUDIT-1 S16.7). The journal filter is the same toggle-button group but re-keys and replaces the <ol> silently, so the result of the toggle is invisible to a screen reader.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader user presses «رحلات» in the category filter. The list below changes to two posts, but nothing is spoken, so they cannot tell whether anything happened or how many posts match.
suggested_fix:
Add `

{`${category}: ${shown.length}`}

` next to the filter, mirroring SceneGallery.

title: Spelling errors in published contact copy
claim: The services intro and one service line contain orthographic errors: «الإستشارة» (hamza on a wasl alif; correct «الاستشارة»), «الاتقان» (correct «الإتقان») and «المتابعه» (final ه for ة; correct «المتابعة»). The text is Anas's own deck copy, so it may need his confirmation, but as shipped these are wrong Arabic on a public page (/contact, «الاستشارات»).
failure_scenario: Visitors to /contact read «الإستشارة» and «المتابعه» in the consulting section; the mistakes are on the page that sells the consulting service.
suggested_fix: Correct to «الاستشارة», «الإتقان», «المتابعة» (line 14) and confirm the wording with Anas.
